evidence: Finding: review-highload F-001 (raw/review-highload-w1.txt), tree re-read fan-out vs the fail-fast read permit. Site-check at head 9f4ec475bd93ff0a9d64c648ebc3c247cfd73a3a (git rev-parse HEAD; git status clean under apps/desktop). Every named site exists as described: MetaprojectTree.tsx:26-50 flatten pushes every visible parent with no folder entry into `unread` (:32); :96-98 the effect calls `model.ensure(scope, parent)` for all of them in one pass. useMetaprojectTree.ts:78-82 a snapshot change keeps `expanded` and drops all folders; :154-158 ensure marks loading then calls read; :114-122 read calls `send(root, input)` with no limiter or queue. platform/metaproject.ts:284-301 requestMetaprojectTree -> invoke("metaproject_request") with no limiter; an `unavailable: ...` reason becomes MetaprojectRequestError("unavailable", ...) (:297-299), which useMetaprojectTree.ts:147-150 stores as a terminal folder error; the reveal/unread paths never re-read a failed folder (flatten :36-38 pushes no unread for status failed), so only per-row Retry (:168-172) recovers. metaproject.rs:185-200 `static ACTIVE: AtomicUsize`, `const MAX_ACTIVE: usize = 8`, acquire returns Err("unavailable: Too many Metaproject reads. Retry shortly.") instead of waiting; :308 every v2 request takes one permit before spawn_blocking, held until cli_response's child exits (150 s cap, :208). No cancellation of retired-generation reads exists (read only checks current() after the answer, :123/:135). git blame -L 184,200 metaproject.rs: the permit lines come from 904fd138a/7ac21ddc7 (pre-existing, not in this diff; the diff adds 46 lines elsewhere in the file), so the defect is the new unbounded client fan-out meeting a pre-existing fail-fast bound. keryx ctx rg --all 'ReadPermit::acquire|MAX_ACTIVE' apps/desktop/src-tauri/src: one call site in metaproject.rs (:308). The DOM tests' reader double has no permit, so nothing at head exercises >8 concurrent tree reads. Nothing was executed (this pass runs no tests; no Rust toolchain locally), so the 9th-read refusal and the resulting error rows are not reproduced; the check establishes the code shape, not the behaviour. Red test that would make this confirmed: in MetaprojectTree.dom.test.tsx (or useMetaprojectTree's test), a reader that holds every request and records the peak number in flight; render with 9+ expanded top-level folders, change the snapshot, release the root page, and assert peak in-flight tree reads <= a bound (e.g. 3) — at this head the peak equals the number of expanded siblings. Pair with a reader that rejects the 9th concurrent call with 'unavailable: Too many Metaproject reads. Retry shortly.' and assert no row reads 'Could not load'. Severity: the finding names a trigger (7-8+ expanded siblings when the snapshot changes, plus concurrent explorer reads) and an observable outcome (persistent error rows, failed detail/neighbors reads), so `major` fits the canonical rubric; it is none of the four blocker shapes.

Finding: review-logic F-001 (raw/review-logic-w1.txt), Home on the first row / End on the last row leaves focusRequest pending. Site-check at head 9f4ec475bd93ff0a9d64c648ebc3c247cfd73a3a. Named site exists: MetaprojectTree.tsx:155-159 moveTo does setFocusId(row.id) then focusRequest.current = true; keryx ctx read of the full file shows it is the only writer of `focusRequest.current = true`; the only reader is the dependency-free useLayoutEffect :124-135, which clears it and focuses '[role="treeitem"][tabindex="0"]' on whatever commit runs next. onFocus (:219) and the click handlers (:194, :199) keep focusId equal to the focused row, so Home (:171, moveTo(rows[0])) on the first row and End (:172, moveTo(rows.at(-1))) on the last row call setFocusId with the current value; onKeyDown changes no other state on those keys. Arrow keys cannot hit the same row (index±1; ArrowRight to a child; ArrowLeft to a lower level; out-of-range returns at :156), so the site list of one (`:155`) is complete. The reveal effect (:101-122) calls model.setHandled on a selection made elsewhere, which re-renders the tree (useMetaprojectTree.ts:86-91, :188-190) and would run the layout effect. Tests: keryx ctx rg --all over MetaprojectTree.dom.test.tsx finds Home/End only at :209/:211, each moving to a different row (End from 'src' to README.md, Home from README.md to docs), and the focus-not-stolen assertions (:236, :283) never follow a same-row Home/End. Nothing was executed (this pass runs no tests), so the claim's premise — that React skips the commit (and thus the layout effect) for a same-value setFocusId — is not reproduced here. Red test that would make this confirmed: in MetaprojectTree.dom.test.tsx, render the Harness, focus item('docs') (rows[0]), await key(item('docs'), 'Home'), focus an outside button, then cause a tree commit with no keyboard input (re-render the Harness with selection/selected set to another node, or release a held folder read) and expect(document.activeElement).toBe(outside); at this head it should fail if the finding holds. Severity: the finding names a trigger (Home on the first row / End on the last, then any data or selection render) and an observable outcome (keyboard focus moved into the tree, against AC6 'without moving focus'), so `major` fits the canonical rubric; not a blocker shape.
